arguments.heading: What happened at the argument

the side that brought the case's advocate noted that the lower court did not hold that the prisoner was entitled to new counsel.
the side that brought the case's advocate mentioned that the prisoner's habeas corpus petition was litigated before the same judge for twelve years.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case concerns a prisoner who asked a federal judge to replace his court-appointed lawyer. The judge denied the request without holding a hearing. The prisoner claims this process was unfair. The government claims the judge acted within their authority.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 27, lines 38-6

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on December 6, 2011.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 8-16

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Supreme Court to require a hearing before a judge denies a request to change lawyers.
the opposing side wants the Supreme Court to allow judges to deny requests to change lawyers without holding a hearing.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 27, lines 38-6

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that a judge must hold a hearing to investigate the specific reasons for the request before denying it.
the opposing side argues that a judge has broad discretion to deny a request to change lawyers without holding a hearing.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked whether the lower court's decision was wrong under any standard of review.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines the minimum procedural steps a judge must take before denying a request to change lawyers. It affects how courts handle disputes between prisoners and their court-appointed attorneys. It shapes the balance between judicial efficiency and the right to effective legal representation.
